# An algorithm through codespec

Generated by `codespec-docs` from the checked-in files of [`examples/series`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/tree/main/examples/series); `task examples` writes them and `task check` fails when any of them, or this page, drifts. [`greeter`](/docs/examples/greeter) shows the pipeline step by step; this page shows where an algorithm's Go and Rust differ and what codespec writes there.

## The package

`series` holds a slice of `int` and 18 functions: insertion sort, median, a sliding window, gcd, Collatz steps, trial-division primes and two `switch` classifications. The Go reader reads it into one `cir/1` module with 0 refusals; the Rust writer writes it with no refusal:

```json title="examples/series/out/rust/refusals.json"
[]
```

<details>
<summary>The whole source, 245 lines</summary>

```go title="examples/series/source/series.go"
// Package series keeps a list of integer samples and computes statistics over it.
package series

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

type Trend string

const (
	Flat    Trend = "flat"
	Rising  Trend = "rising"
	Falling Trend = "falling"
	Mixed   Trend = "mixed"
)

const maxSteps = 1000

var ErrEmpty = errors.New("series is empty")

var ErrBadWindow = errors.New("window must be positive")

type Series struct {
	values []int
}

func New() *Series {
	return &Series{values: []int{}}
}

// Push appends v and returns the new length.
func (s *Series) Push(v int) int {
	s.values = append(s.values, v)
	return len(s.values)
}

// Sum adds every value; the sum wraps on overflow.
func (s *Series) Sum() int {
	total := 0
	for _, v := range s.values {
		total += v
	}
	return total
}

func (s *Series) Mean() (int, error) {
	if len(s.values) == 0 {
		return 0, ErrEmpty
	}
	return s.Sum() / len(s.values), nil
}

// Sorted returns the values in ascending order, by insertion sort; the series is unchanged.
func (s *Series) Sorted() []int {
	out := []int{}
	for _, v := range s.values {
		out = append(out, v)
	}
	for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
		x := out[i]
		j := i - 1
		for j >= 0 && out[j] > x {
			out[j+1] = out[j]
			j--
		}
		out[j+1] = x
	}
	return out
}

func (s *Series) Median() (int, error) {
	n := len(s.values)
	if n == 0 {
		return 0, ErrEmpty
	}
	sorted := s.Sorted()
	if n%2 == 1 {
		return sorted[n/2], nil
	}
	return (sorted[n/2-1] + sorted[n/2]) / 2, nil
}

// Reverse reverses the series in place.
func (s *Series) Reverse() {
	for i, j := 0, len(s.values)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		s.values[i], s.values[j] = s.values[j], s.values[i]
	}
}

func (s *Series) Trend() Trend {
	up := 0
	down := 0
	for i := 1; i < len(s.values); i++ {
		switch {
		case s.values[i] > s.values[i-1]:
			up++
		case s.values[i] < s.values[i-1]:
			down++
		}
	}
	switch {
	case up > 0 && down > 0:
		return Mixed
	case up > 0:
		return Rising
	case down > 0:
		return Falling
	}
	return Flat
}

// MaxWindow is the largest sum of w consecutive values.
func (s *Series) MaxWindow(w int) (int, error) {
	if w <= 0 {
		return 0, ErrBadWindow
	}
	if w > len(s.values) {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("window %d is longer than the series (%d)", w, len(s.values))
	}
	cur := 0
	for i := 0; i < w; i++ {
		cur += s.values[i]
	}
	best := cur
	for i := w; i < len(s.values); i++ {
		cur += s.values[i] - s.values[i-w]
		if cur > best {
			best = cur
		}
	}
	return best, nil
}

// Gcd is the greatest common divisor of every value, 0 for an empty series.
func (s *Series) Gcd() int {
	g := 0
	for _, v := range s.values {
		g = gcd(g, v)
	}
	return g
}

func gcd(a int, b int) int {
	if a < 0 {
		a = -a
	}
	if b < 0 {
		b = -b
	}
	for b != 0 {
		a, b = b, a%b
	}
	return a
}

// EvenSum adds the even values.
func (s *Series) EvenSum() int {
	total := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s.values); i++ {
		if s.values[i]%2 != 0 {
			continue
		}
		total += s.values[i]
	}
	return total
}

// Drop removes every value equal to v and returns how many it removed.
func (s *Series) Drop(v int) int {
	kept := []int{}
	removed := 0
	for _, x := range s.values {
		if x == v {
			removed++
			continue
		}
		kept = append(kept, x)
	}
	s.values = kept
	return removed
}

func (s *Series) Len() int {
	return len(s.values)
}

// Steps counts the Collatz steps from n to 1, stopping at maxSteps.
func Steps(n int) (int, error) {
	if n <= 0 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("steps of %d: n must be positive", n)
	}
	steps := 0
	for n != 1 {
		if n%2 == 0 {
			n /= 2
		} else {
			n = 3*n + 1
		}
		steps++
		if steps == maxSteps {
			break
		}
	}
	return steps, nil
}

func IsPrime(n int) bool {
	if n < 2 {
		return false
	}
	for d := 2; d <= n/d; d++ {
		if n%d == 0 {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// Bucket names the size class of v.
func Bucket(v int) string {
	switch {
	case v < 0:
		return "negative"
	case v == 0:
		return "zero"
	case v < 10:
		return "small"
	case v < 1000:
		return "medium"
	}
	return "large"
}

// Residue names v modulo 3, with Go's sign: the remainder takes the sign of v.
func Residue(v int) string {
	switch v % 3 {
	case 0:
		return "divisible"
	case 1, -2:
		return "one-over"
	default:
		return "one-under"
	}
}
```

## Go and the Rust written from it

### `for` with `break`: Collatz steps

A condition-only `for` is a `cir/1` `for` with only `cond`; the Rust writer makes it a `while`. `3*n + 1` overflows `int64` for large `n`; Go wraps, so Rust uses `wrapping_mul` and `wrapping_add`. `steps` is renamed `steps_` because a local may not shadow the function.

```go title="source/series.go"
func Steps(n int) (int, error) {
	if n <= 0 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("steps of %d: n must be positive", n)
	}
	steps := 0
	for n != 1 {
		if n%2 == 0 {
			n /= 2
		} else {
			n = 3*n + 1
		}
		steps++
		if steps == maxSteps {
			break
		}
	}
	return steps, nil
}
```

```rust title="out/rust/src/lib.rs"
pub fn steps(mut n: i64) -> Result<i64, Error> {
    if n <= 0i64 {
        return Err(Error::Msg(format!("steps of {}: n must be positive", n)));
    }
    let mut steps_ = 0i64;
    while n != 1i64 {
        if n.wrapping_rem(2i64) == 0i64 {
            n = n.wrapping_div(2i64);
        } else {
            n = 3i64.wrapping_mul(n).wrapping_add(1i64);
        }
        steps_ = steps_.wrapping_add(1i64);
        if steps_ == MAX_STEPS {
            break;
        }
    }
    Ok(steps_)
}
```

### `continue` in a three-clause `for`: `post` runs first

Go runs `i++` before the next test when `continue` skips the rest of the body. Rust's `while` has no post statement, so the writer puts `post` at the end of the body and again before every `continue`.

```go title="source/series.go"
func (s *Series) EvenSum() int {
	total := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s.values); i++ {
		if s.values[i]%2 != 0 {
			continue
		}
		total += s.values[i]
	}
	return total
}
```

```rust title="out/rust/src/lib.rs"
    pub fn even_sum(&self) -> i64 {
        let mut total = 0i64;
        {
            let mut i = 0i64;
            while i < self.values.len() as i64 {
                if self.values[i as usize].wrapping_rem(2i64) != 0i64 {
                    {
                        i = i.wrapping_add(1i64);
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                total = total.wrapping_add(self.values[i as usize]);
                i = i.wrapping_add(1i64);
            }
        }
        total
    }
```

### Swap: every value read before any target is written

`a, b = b, a` in Go evaluates both right-hand sides first. The writer binds each value to a fresh `__value` local and then assigns the targets in order, for the swap and for the two-variable post statement.

```go title="source/series.go"
func (s *Series) Reverse() {
	for i, j := 0, len(s.values)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		s.values[i], s.values[j] = s.values[j], s.values[i]
	}
}
```

```rust title="out/rust/src/lib.rs"
    pub fn reverse(&mut self) {
        {
            let (mut i, mut j) = (0i64, (self.values.len() as i64).wrapping_sub(1i64));
            while i < j {
                {
                    let __value0 = self.values[j as usize];
                    let __value1 = self.values[i as usize];
                    self.values[i as usize] = __value0;
                    self.values[j as usize] = __value1;
                }
                {
                    let __value0 = i.wrapping_add(1i64);
                    let __value1 = j.wrapping_sub(1i64);
                    i = __value0;
                    j = __value1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
```

### `switch` with a tag, and Go's remainder sign

The tag is evaluated once into `__tag`; each `case` list becomes an `||` chain. Go's `%` takes the sign of the dividend, as Rust's `wrapping_rem` does, so `-2` is a case of its own.

```go title="source/series.go"
func Residue(v int) string {
	switch v % 3 {
	case 0:
		return "divisible"
	case 1, -2:
		return "one-over"
	default:
		return "one-under"
	}
}
```

```rust title="out/rust/src/lib.rs"
pub fn residue(v: i64) -> String {
    {
        let __tag = v.wrapping_rem(3i64);
        if __tag == 0i64 {
            return String::from("divisible");
        } else if __tag == 1i64 || __tag == 2i64.wrapping_neg() {
            return String::from("one-over");
        } else {
            return String::from("one-under");
        }
    }
}
```

	total := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s.values); i++ {
		if s.values[i]%2 != 0 {
			continue
		}
		total += s.values[i]
	}
	return total
}

// Drop removes every value equal to v and returns how many it removed.
func (s *Series) Drop(v int) int {
	kept := []int{}
	removed := 0
	for _, x := range s.values {
		if x == v {
			removed++
			continue
		}
		kept = append(kept, x)
	}
	s.values = kept
	return removed
}

func (s *Series) Len() int {
	return len(s.values)
}

// Steps counts the Collatz steps from n to 1, stopping at maxSteps.
func Steps(n int) (int, error) {
	if n <= 0 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("steps of %d: n must be positive", n)
	}
	steps := 0
	for n != 1 {
		if n%2 == 0 {
			n /= 2
		} else {
			n = 3*n + 1
		}
		steps++
		if steps == maxSteps {
			break
		}
	}
	return steps, nil
}

func IsPrime(n int) bool {
	if n < 2 {
		return false
	}
	for d := 2; d <= n/d; d++ {
		if n%d == 0 {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// Bucket names the size class of v.
func Bucket(v int) string {
	switch {
	case v < 0:
		return "negative"
	case v == 0:
		return "zero"
	case v < 10:
		return "small"
	case v < 1000:
		return "medium"
	}
	return "large"
}

// Residue names v modulo 3, with Go's sign: the remainder takes the sign of v.
func Residue(v int) string {
	switch v % 3 {
	case 0:
		return "divisible"
	case 1, -2:
		return "one-over"
	default:
		return "one-under"
	}
}
